terms.comment: Lewis & Short gives it as a noun, “a gaming-house”, from Sidonius, a writer of the fifth century; it is built on the classical āleātor, a dice-player. The adjective āleātōrius is Cicero’s (āleātōria damna, Cic. Phil. 2.27, as Lewis & Short cites it).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 287.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
